title: Twisting sheaves on the projective line: invertibility, tensor powers, non-vanishing loci
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading, $P=\operatorname{Proj}S$ as in [def-sc-p1-standard], and for $n\in\mathbf Z$ let $\mathcal O_P(n)=\widetilde{S(n)}$ be the twist of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], with $x_0,x_1\in\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P(1))$ the global sections given by (3) of that node. For $n,m\in\mathbf Z$ let $\mu_{n,m}:\mathcal O_P(n)\otimes_{\mathcal O_P}\mathcal O_P(m)\to\mathcal O_P(n+m)$ be the multiplication map, given on each standard open $D_+(f)$ by $(a/f^r)\otimes(b/f^q)\mapsto ab/f^{r+q}$ in $S_f$. Then: (1) $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_P$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and every $\mu_{n,m}$ is an isomorphism; consequently, for every $\mathcal O_P$-module $\mathcal G$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$ there is an isomorphism $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(n)$ (for $n<0$, $\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes n}$ is the $(-n)$-th tensor power of the dual of $\mathcal O_P(1)$), and these isomorphisms carry the maps $t\mapsto t\otimes x_i$ from degree $n$ to degree $n+1$ on the left to the maps $t\mapsto\mu(t\otimes x_i)$ on the right, $i=0,1$; (2) for $i=0,1$ the open set $P_{x_i}=\{x\in P: x_i(x)\ne0\text{ in }\mathcal O_P(1)_x\otimes\kappa(x)\}$ where $x_i$ does not vanish equals $D_+(x_i)$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01MS (lemma-when-invertible) with d=1 and f=x_0,x_1, Lemma 01MU (lemma-where-invertible: W_1=P since D_+(x_i)=D_+(x_i\cdot 1) with deg x_i = deg 1 + 1), Lemma 01MV (lemma-principal-open, n=d=1) for (2); Lemma 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space) for the cover

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proj-polynomial-twist-chart] with $A=k$, $m=1$ (only its clauses on the cover and on functions are used, not its glued module): $U_0=D_+(x_0)$ and $U_1=D_+(x_1)$ cover $P$, $\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_P)=S_{(x_i)}$, and for $i\ne j$, $U_i\cap U_j$ is the basic open of the function $x_i/x_j$ in $U_j$. By (2) of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ and every homogeneous $f$ of positive degree with $D_+(f)\subseteq U_i$, $\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal O_P(n))=(S_f)_n$ is free of rank one over $S_{(f)}$ with basis $x_i^n/1$ (elementary: $x_i$ is a unit of $S_f$, so $c=(c\,x_i^{-n})\cdot x_i^n$ with $c\,x_i^{-n}\in S_{(f)}$, uniquely), compatibly with the restriction maps, which are localization maps. Hence $a\mapsto a\cdot x_i^n$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{U_i}\to\mathcal O_P(n)|_{U_i}$; in particular $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is quasi-coherent (by construction) and locally free of rank one, i.e. invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], with generator $x_i$ (the global section of (3) of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], equal to $x_i/1$ on every $D_+(f)$) on $U_i$. This is the computation of Stacks 01MS with $d=1$, $f=x_i$.

Being a morphism of sheaves, $\mu_{n,m}$ is an isomorphism if its restrictions to $U_0$ and $U_1$ are. On $U_i$, by Step 1, $\mathcal O_P(n)|_{U_i}\otimes\mathcal O_P(m)|_{U_i}$ is free of rank one with basis $x_i^n\otimes x_i^m$, and $\mu_{n,m}$ sends it to $x_i^nx_i^m=x_i^{n+m}$, the basis of $\mathcal O_P(n+m)|_{U_i}$; so $\mu_{n,m}|_{U_i}$ is an isomorphism (Stacks 01MS). Consequently: for $n\ge0$ the iterated multiplication $\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes n}\to\mathcal O_P(n)$ is an isomorphism (induction on $n$ via $\mu_{n,1}$); $\mu_{1,-1}:\mathcal O_P(1)\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)\to\mathcal O_P$ is an isomorphism of invertible modules, so its adjoint $\mathcal O_P(-1)\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_P(1),\mathcal O_P)=\mathcal O_P(1)^\vee$ is an isomorphism (on $U_i$ it sends the basis $x_i^{-1}$ to the dual basis of $x_i$), and for $n<0$ iterating $\mu_{-1,-1}$ gives $(\mathcal O_P(1)^\vee)^{\otimes(-n)}\cong\mathcal O_P(n)$. Tensoring with $\mathcal G$ gives $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(n)$. Under these isomorphisms $t\otimes x_i$ goes to $\mu(t\otimes x_i)$ by associativity of multiplication in $S_f$ (for $n<0$ also using that the dual pairing is $\mu_{1,-1}$). Elementary: a check on the bases over the two charts.

Let $x\in P$. If $x\in U_i$, then $x_i$ is a free generator of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ near $x$ (Step 1), so its image in $\mathcal O_P(1)_x\otimes\kappa(x)\cong\kappa(x)$ is nonzero. If $x\in U_j$, $j\ne i$, then on $U_j$ we have $x_i=(x_i/x_j)\cdot x_j$ with $x_j$ a free generator, so $x_i$ does not vanish at $x$ iff the function $x_i/x_j$ does not vanish at $x$, iff $x$ lies in the basic open of $x_i/x_j$ in $U_j$, which is $U_i\cap U_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-polynomial-twist-chart]. Since $U_0\cup U_1=P$, $P_{x_i}=D_+(x_i)$ (Stacks 01MV with $n=d=1$). Elementary.
